steps.text: That access mask looks like PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION requested via lsm.dll, which is typical benign Local Session Manager behavior — I should verify the source process before flagging it.

steps.text: This looks benign—the svchost GUID has a low sequence number (0x12) and started near boot time close to lsass, which is consistent with normal behavior.
I'm marking this alert as benign — svchost.exe on workstation5 made a routine status query to lsass.exe via the Local Session Manager service, with no attempt to access LSASS memory or credentials.

submission.reasoning: On workstation5, svchost.exe (C:\windows\system32\svchost.exe, started at boot just after lsass) opened a handle to the real lsass.exe (C:\windows\system32\lsass.exe) at 2020-10-23T06:36:43Z. It happened 6 times in about 0.5s. The access rights were 0x1000 (PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION), which cannot read process memory, so a credential dump is not possible with this handle. The call trace runs through RPCRT4 into lsm.dll (Local Session Manager) and then KERNELBASE/ntdll. That pattern fits the Local Session Manager service answering an RPC request about a session. There are no read-memory rights, no unknown DLLs or unbacked code in the stack, and the image path is the normal system one. This is routine OS behaviour, not credential theft.
